predecessors.note: Kai Province, where the Takeda 'controlled Kai Province at the close of the Heian period' and Harunobu (Shingen) succeeded as shugo in 1540 (Takeda clan page). Cliopatria's Warring States Japan row draws all Japan as one shape; the daimyo domains are internal units.

union.text: western Kōzuke around Minowa and Kuragano

land.text: the Takeda lands that the Oda-Tokugawa alliance overran in March 1582

successors.note: Katsuyori page: the Oda-Tokugawa alliance advanced into Kai and destroyed the clan in March 1582; the page does not divide the lands (Suruga went to Tokugawa Ieyasu, Kai, Shinano and Kōzuke to the Oda in other accounts).

capitals.name: Kōfu (Kai Province)
capitals.note: The Takeda page names Kai as the home province; the seat at Kōfu is the researcher's placement, no page opened names it.

capitals.name: Shinpu Castle (Nirasaki)
capitals.note: Katsuyori 'had moved his residence to Shinpu Castle' in 1581; he set fire to it in 1582. The coordinates are the researcher's placement.

rulers.name: Takeda Shingen (Harunobu)
rulers.note: Infobox 1541-1573; text: 'He succeeded in 1540'; took the name Shingen in 1559; died 13 May 1573.

rulers.name: Takeda Katsuyori
rulers.note: Died 11 March 1582 after Tenmokuzan, the clan's end.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for a daimyo domain Cliopatria lacks (Warring States Japan draws all of Japan as one shape). Home province Kai (Yamanashi, about 4,800 km2 by the gazetteer); Harunobu succeeded as shugo of Kai in 1540. The Shinano castles of 1543-1550 (Nagakubo, Takatō, Uchiyama, Fukashi) are on the Shingen page without a province; the Sengoku page dates the rule of Shinano from 1553, so the shape stays Kai until then.

The Sengoku page: Shingen 'ruled Kai and Shinano Provinces from 1553 to 1573'. Nagano Prefecture (about 15,400 km2) stands for Shinano; the northern end around the Kawanakajima plain was fought over with Uesugi Kenshin 1553-1564 (a contest in the ledger). No page gives an area.

union.text: western Kōzuke around Minowa and Kuragano

keyframe_review.note: 1565: Shingen 'took Kuragano and Minowa Castles in Kōzuke'; a 35 km circle at Minowa (about 4,300 km2) is the researcher's reading of the holding.

union.text: western Kōzuke around Minowa and Kuragano

correction.text: Kai, Shinano, western Kōzuke and Suruga

keyframe_review.note: 1569: Shingen 'secured Suruga after defeating Hōjō Ujimasa's forces' (the page's wording); a 45 km circle at Shizuoka stands for Suruga. In 1572 Akiyama Nobutomo's forces took Iwamura Castle in Mino and Shingen took Futamata Castle from Tokugawa; in 1573 he entered Mikawa and died: those are raids, not drawn.

union.text: western Kōzuke around Minowa and Kuragano

correction.text: the lands above plus Takatenjin in Tōtōmi

keyframe_review.note: 1574: Katsuyori captured Takatenjin 'which even his father had not managed to do'; the page does not name the province (Tōtōmi) or the extent. Takeda rule peaked in these years (Takeda clan page: 'briefly achieved the largest extent of Takeda rule').

union.text: western Kōzuke around Minowa and Kuragano

correction.text: Kai, Shinano, western Kōzuke and Suruga

keyframe_review.note: 1581: Katsuyori 'lost Takatenjin fortress to Tokugawa Ieyasu' and moved to Shinpu Castle; the clan's end came in March 1582.

ledger.note: 1540: Takeda Harunobu (Shingen) takes the Takeda. 'Takeda Harunobu succeeded his father Nobutora as shugo of Kai' (Takeda clan page); the Shingen page: a bloodless coup against Nobutora, who was sent into custody in Suruga under the Imagawa (infobox head of the clan from 1541).

1553: Shinano is Takeda. The Sengoku page: Shingen 'ruled Kai and Shinano Provinces from 1553 to 1573'; the Shingen page lists the castles taken from 1543 (Nagakubo, Kojinyama, Takatō, Ryūgasaki, Uchiyama, Shika, Fukashi), the 1548 defeat of Ogasawara Nagatoki at Shiojiritoge, and Murakami Yoshikiyo's check at Uedahara (undated); the provinces are not named there.

region.text: the Kawanakajima plain in northern Shinano

ledger.note: 1553: Kawanakajima. Uesugi Kenshin 'fought in the Battle of Kawanakajima five times between 1553 and 1564' against Shingen; the Takeda clan page puts the best-known battle on 10 September 1561. The page does not name the ground; the Kawanakajima plain in northern Shinano is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the Kawanakajima plain in northern Shinano

ledger.note: 1564: the last Kawanakajima. The page gives 1553 to 1564 for the five battles; no treaty is on the pages.

region.text: western Kōzuke around Minowa and Kuragano

ledger.note: 1565: western Kōzuke. Shingen 'took Kuragano and Minowa Castles in Kōzuke'; in 1567 he secured 'a castle in western Kōzuke'. The previous holders are not named on the page.

region.text: Suruga Province, invaded by Takeda in 1568

ledger.note: 1568: Shingen invades Suruga. In 1567 he and Tokugawa Ieyasu 'came to terms and occupied former Imagawa territory'; in 1568 he broke with the Hōjō, moved into Musashi and besieged Hachigata and Odawara (the Hōjō page: after Imagawa Yoshimoto's death at Okehazama in 1560 he planned the invasion).

region.text: eastern Suruga around Fukazawa Castle, where the Hōjō intervened

ledger.note: 1568: the Hōjō against Takeda Shingen. 'Shingen entered Musashi in response to Hōjō intervention in his invasion of Suruga'; Odawara's town burned in 1569 and the Hōjō won at Mimasetoge; Katsuyori besieged Kanbara in 1569.
1569: Suruga secured. 'Secured Suruga after defeating Hōjō Ujimasa's forces' (the Shingen page); the Hōjō page: 'Takeda Katsuyori besieged Kanbara Castle in Suruga' in 1569.

1569: Suruga Province is Takeda land. The Shingen page's year; the Imagawa, whose lord Yoshimoto died at Okehazama in 1560, are the previous holders (the page gives the occupation of 'former Imagawa territory' in 1567 with Tokugawa Ieyasu).
1571: Fukazawa. 'Shingen took Fukazawa Castle in Suruga' (Hōjō Ujiyasu page); Ujiyasu died that year.

1572: Shingen against Tokugawa Ieyasu. Akiyama Nobutomo's forces took Iwamura Castle in Mino; 'Shingen later captured Tokugawa's Futamata Castle'; in 1573, urged by Ashikaga Yoshiaki, he fought at Mikatagahara, entered Mikawa with over 30,000 men and besieged Noda Castle.
1574: Takatenjin. Katsuyori 'captured Takatenjin castle, which even his father had not managed to do'; the page does not name the province or the previous holder (the Tokugawa clan was his enemy).
1581: Takatenjin falls to Tokugawa Ieyasu. 'He lost Takatenjin fortress to Tokugawa Ieyasu, and 680 men of Okabe Motonobu's garrison died in the siege.'
1581: the Tōtōmi front closes with the loss of Takatenjin; the page gives no peace.

union.text: western Kōzuke around Minowa and Kuragano

ledger.note: 11 March 1582: the Takeda end. Takato fell to Oda Nobutada on 2 March; the Oda-Tokugawa alliance advanced into Kai, Katsuyori burned Shinpu Castle and fled to Tenmoku mountain, where his forces were destroyed and he, his wife and his son 'committed seppuku'; the page: this ended the Takeda clan.

wars.name: Battles of Kawanakajima

zones.text: the Kawanakajima plain in northern Shinano

wars.outcome: Five battles without decision; the Takeda kept Shinano, the Uesugi stayed in Echigo.
wars.note: The Takeda clan page puts the fiercest on 10 September 1561.

wars.name: Takeda invasion of Suruga
wars.outcome: Takeda secured Suruga in 1569 after defeating the Hōjō; the Hōjō won at Mimasetoge in 1569; Fukazawa fell in 1571.

wars.name: Battle of Mikatagahara and the Mikawa campaign
wars.outcome: Shingen won at Mikatagahara and entered Mikawa with over 30,000 men; he died on 13 May 1573 at Noda and the campaign stopped.

wars.name: Battle of Nagashino
wars.outcome: Katsuyori's defeat to Nobunaga's volley fire of about 3,000 muskets; 'the clan declined afterward' (Takeda clan page). No land changed at once.

wars.name: Oda–Tokugawa invasion of Kai
wars.outcome: Takato fell on 2 March 1582, Shinpu was burned and Katsuyori died at Tenmokuzan on 11 March 1582; the Takeda clan ended.

certainty.note: The pages name castles, provinces and a plain; the Echigo, Hōjō and Tokugawa frontiers shifted each campaign.

notes: Written by jk-01-x on 2026-10-19 from five pages (Takeda clan, Takeda Shingen, Takeda Katsuyori, Hōjō Ujiyasu, Sengoku period). A Sengoku daimyo domain inside Cliopatria's single Warring States Japan row. Kai is the home province; every other land is dated by the Sengoku or Shingen pages (Shinano from 1553, Kōzuke 1565, Suruga 1569, Takatenjin 1574-1581) and drawn with prefectures or circles. Not on the pages: Hida, Mikawa and Tōtōmi holdings beyond Takatenjin, the Suwa conquest (1542), the 1554 Kai-Sagami-Suruga alliance (the Sengoku page has it as the Takeda-Hōjō-Imagawa alliance formed in 1554), the Kawanakajima ground, the division of the Takeda lands in 1582 (successor: oda-clan, to be written; Suruga to Tokugawa Ieyasu and the Kōshin lands in the Tenshō-Jingo war are in other accounts). Counterpart strings 'Shinano lords (Ogasawara, Murakami and others)', 'imagawa-clan' (no dossier; the Imagawa fall in 1560, the page names Yoshimoto), 'tokugawa-clan' (written in this batch; Ieyasu's domain until October 1600). Capital at Kōfu is the researcher's placement. The Hōjō Ujiyasu page says 'Hōjō Ujimasa's forces' in the Suruga fighting (Ujimasa as the Takeda page puts it). Area comparison not applicable (no infobox area).
